questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a friend but had the impression that it was also possible to find housing on your own through Idealista, which I also used myself last year in Almería.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive (especially if you're an exchange student) and you have to make sure you get a proper contract. But it's definitely worth living off campus if you go to Universidad Autonoma de Barcelona like I did, since the housing on campus (the Vila) is placed right next to the university which means you'll be living in Bellaterra, 45 minutes by train from Barcelona. I really recommend living in the city instead of on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult because UAB doesn't sign the OLA in the digital system, which means you have to download the pdf and send it manually to them. I didn't realize this until very late, so I ended up getting my Erasmus rant quite late into my exchange.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact Intercanvis Lletres

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to send the OLA manually on mail after having received the signature from your sending institution. Go to all the classes that you chose the first week to find out if they fit your schedule and if you like the teacher, exam method, work load etc. If not, try out alternative classes and decide as fast as possible which ones to follow, preferably in the first couple of weeks so you don't miss to much. Be aware of the period of changing enrollment that UAB has (you'll be informed about this on the Introduction day, so show up for that).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is a bit more difficult because of the "language barrier", I had all my courses in Spanish which was fine but sometimes a bit harder to follow compared to back home. Also I experienced the work load as way bigger than in UCPH. In UAB, a course of 6 ECTS points will have as much or more reading, more exams etc. than a course of 15 ECTS points in the UCPH, and in addition to that everything is in Spanish. Last year on exchange I did 5 courses of 6 ECTS points which was very busy and in exam periods quite stressfull. This year I did 3 courses of 6 ECTS points and my bachelor thesis at the same time, which I wouldn't recommend (I've ended up prolonging my bachelor thesis). 3 courses of 6 ECTS points is busy as well but would have been perfect for me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of learning and teaching is different, the exams are often without any help so it's mostly about remembering all the stuff by heart and writing it down as fast as possible in the exam. Most classes consist of the teacher speaking to the students for 1,5 hour, most of the time with very little or no student participation at all. In my experience, the best way to prepare for the exams was to attend all the classes and try to write down what the teacher says in the class, as some teachers don't use powerpoints or don't upload them to Campus virtual after class. When studying for the exams I would go through all my notes and try to memorize it. The website Wuolah is also very helpful, as students from the exact same courses as you upload their notes in there.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
100023 Literatura Española
106348 Comentario de Textos Literarios
106347 Literatura Española desde el siglo de las luces hasta las Vanguardias

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend 106348 Comentario de Textos Literarios because the teacher I had (Lucia) was very nice, used powerpoints in her classes and didn't do memorizing exams. Instead she did an exam in the end of the semester in which you had to analyze an extract from a text. The course is less theoretical and more practical (meaning you learn how to write a literary commentary), and it doesn't have as many "in-class" exams, instead you have to hand in a couple of papers during the semester. 

I would also to some extent recommend 100023 Literatura Española as I liked the teacher (Rebecca), but there is a lot of reading to do in this subject (you have to read the first part of the Quijote, a novel and some theater plays) which can be challenging if Spanish is not your native language. If you do choose this subject I'd recommend to start reading the obligatory readings when you start the course basically, so that it doesn't get too stressfull in the end.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the city (and the nature around it), it has endless opportunities to offer. Take the train down or up the coast to the smaller villages. Go to other Spanish cities with public transportation or rent a car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any challenges adjusting

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really find any of the differences challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, especially if you speak Spanish, the food, the music, the nightlife, just the city in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live in the city center, not on campus. 

If you only have 3 courses, try to schedule them so that you don't have to go to the uni every day of the week (you can schedule it so that you only have to go 2 or 3 days a week) if you live in the city center. It's a 40 minutes train ride from Plaza Catalunya, so you could end up spending a lot of time on transportation.

ENJOY it, don't stress it too much (even if you fail a course, it's all going to work out in the end) and speak as much Spanish as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any more

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a bunch of amazing people and getting to explore an incredible city and improve my Spanish. I had the best time there (despite academic and bureaucratic challenges) and would recommend going x 1000.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being unsure if I was able to pass some of the courses, which was quite stressfull at times. Also writing my bachelor thesis while I was there, which I wouldn't recommend to anyone. For me it would have been better to just do courses there and be able to focus on them only.
